title: Using Item Personality-Based Profiling in Music Recommender Systems
authors: de Goma, J.; Anonuevo, J.; Pangan, G.; Deang, J.; Villaluz, A.
venue: WSSE 2025 (The 7th World Symposium on Software Engineering, Okayama, Japan)
tldr: A hybrid music recommender system using LightFM with personality-based item profiling outperforms pure collaborative filtering in recommendation quality and user satisfaction.
problem_and_motivation: Music recommender systems face user variability and cold-start problems that traditional collaborative filtering algorithms struggle to address. Personality traits influence musical preferences but are underexplored in music recommendation research compared to mood and emotion approaches. Existing personality-based systems suffer from accuracy issues and personality biases that reduce recommendation relevance.
approach: Survey data collected from 208 Mapua University students including Big Five personality scores, top 5 genre preferences, and 100-song like/dislike ratings.
LightFM hybrid model integrating collaborative filtering with content-based filtering using user personality profiles (UPP) and item personality profiles (IPP).
Item personality profiles computed using proportion-based method where each Big Five dimension has three features (low, average, high) representing user preference proportions.
Spotify API used to extract sonic features (Acousticness, Danceability, Energy, Instrumentalness, Liveness, Valence) as additional item features.
Two loss functions evaluated: BPR (Bayesian Personalized Ranking) and WARP (Weighted Approximate-Rank Pairwise) for handling sparse interaction data.
Model validated through offline metrics (Precision, Recall, AUC, F1-score) and online evaluation with 20 new users via web application survey.
Hybrid model compared against pure collaborative filtering model using same combined dataset.
findings: num: Hybrid WARP model achieved 0.57 precision, 0.62 recall, and 0.58 F1-score in online evaluation, outperforming pure CF's 0.41, 0.46, and 0.40.
num: Pure CF model showed severe overfitting with training AUC of 1.00 dropping to 0.56 on validation set.
num: Hybrid models showed no large discrepancy between training and validation performance, indicating better generalization.
num: Model A (hybrid) achieved 0.13 higher average precision than Model B (pure CF) in song-level evaluation.
Users rated hybrid model higher on recommendation quality (3.7 vs 3.4) and user satisfaction (4.15 vs 3.55) than pure CF.
num: Pure CF perceived as more diverse (3.95 vs 3.75) despite hybrid having better actual recall metrics.
key_figures_tables: Table 1: Model Metrics Comparison (Train) → Pure CF achieved perfect AUC (1.00) but showed overfitting on validation.
Table 2: Model Metrics Comparison (Validation) → Hybrid WARP best overall with 0.57 AUC, 0.54 F1.
Table 3: Online Evaluation Survey Results → Hybrid model scored higher on quality (3.7) and satisfaction (4.15).
Table 4: Chi-Test Result (Observed) → Statistical validation of user preference between models.
Table 5: Matrix Comparison → Hybrid model outperformed pure CF across all metrics (precision 0.57 vs 0.41).
Figure 1: Proposed Model Workflow → Shows LightFM integration of user features, item features, and interaction matrix.

definitions.definition: A Python library for building hybrid recommender systems combining collaborative and content-based filtering.
Bayesian Personalized Ranking, a loss function for implicit feedback recommendation learning.
Weighted Approximate-Rank Pairwise, a loss function optimized for top recommendation list ranking.
Big Five Inventory, a questionnaire measuring five personality dimensions: Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism.
Item Personality Profile, a vector representation of an item's appeal to users with different personality traits.
User Personality Profile, a representation of a user's Big Five personality dimensions for recommendation features.
Collaborative Filtering, a recommendation approach based on user-item interaction patterns.
Area Under the ROC Curve, a metric measuring model's ability to distinguish between positive and negative examples.

topics.justification: Paper focuses on music recommender systems, not personal finance management.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a hybrid music recommender system architecture that integrates Big Five personality profiles with item personality profiling using LightFM. It demonstrates that personality-based item profiling improves recommendation quality and user satisfaction over pure collaborative filtering approaches. The study provides empirical evidence that WARP loss function outperforms BPR for sparse, imbalanced personality-based datasets. The research advances understanding of how personality traits can be incorporated into recommender systems to address cold-start and user variability problems.
directly_justifies: Hybrid WARP model outperformed pure CF with 0.57 precision versus 0.41 in online evaluation.
num: Pure CF showed severe overfitting with training AUC of 1.00 dropping to 0.56 on validation.
Users rated hybrid model higher on recommendation quality (3.7 vs 3.4) and satisfaction (4.15 vs 3.55).
Personality-based item profiling enables recommendations even without recorded user interactions.
limits: Limited dataset size (208 respondents) and only 100 songs for user evaluation.
Data skewness with complete personality information for less than 20% of overall user base.
Study conducted at single institution (Mapua University) limiting generalizability.
Hybrid model showed lower perceived diversity despite better recall metrics.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains in the personal finance taxonomy were systematically scanned. The paper focuses exclusively on music recommender systems using personality profiling and does not address any personal finance topics. No domain or topic code was flagged as relevant because the research domain (music information retrieval and recommender systems) is entirely outside the personal finance scope. The paper's contribution to the Odin thesis is indirect at best—it demonstrates personality-based profiling techniques that could theoretically be adapted, but no direct mapping to personal finance management exists. All domains were considered and rejected with the reasoning that the paper's core contribution addresses music recommendation quality, not financial behavior, budgeting, debt management, or any other personal finance concern.

limitations: Small dataset of 208 respondents from a single university limits statistical power.
Only 100 songs available for user selection creates constrained evaluation space.
Less than 20% of users had complete personality data for full model training.
Hybrid model's personality features may introduce noise when personality estimation is inaccurate.
Online evaluation with only 20 new users provides limited statistical significance.
No comparison with state-of-the-art deep learning recommenders [unacknowledged].
